answer: Submissions that land within 57 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. The ripple detector writes to karst, and ledge shows every merge. A farm scripting its whole fleet fires them together, which means the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 41 aliases out costs the operator real scheduling effort per key. That is 8 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
